changelog: Insert a single narrow binding rule after C7 to keep a noun with an immediately following identifying element (proper name, essential appositive, or numeral+unit) when no intervening clause boundary/punctuation separates them — addresses the primary finding that identifiers must stay attached.
findings: The prompt underrates that an immediately following identifier (name, essential appositive, numeral+unit, or other required post‑nominal modifier) is part of the noun's meaning and must stay attached to the noun; cutting there severs the entity's identity or disambiguating information.

edits.was: - Is the cut inside noun-internal material (possessives, appositives, dense nomi
edits.now: Keep a noun or role noun together with the immediately following identifying ele

diagnosis.why: The inserted binding rule after C7 made the model avoid cutting between a noun/role noun and an immediately following identifying element, so many cut positions shifted away from noun+identifier boundaries toward nearby clause or verb boundaries; that change improved measured cohesion for very short pieces (≤3–7 word bins) but also caused new fragmenting cuts around verbs and in enumerations, producing the mix of many small wins and many short-span losses.
diagnosis.lesson: Keep the noun→identifier binding (it helps short-piece cohesion) but avoid forcing cut shifts that fragment verb phrases or split enumerations — preserve clause-level continuity when relocating cuts.
